# Flyology

> Flyology is an experimental project for contemporary systems programming in Ada. Its runtime, libraries, and tools focus on performance, interoperability, observability, and explicit control from task execution to application interfaces.

Flyology is the umbrella project. Flyology Runtime is its core GNAT runtime extension. Some libraries require the runtime and use its task-aware I/O. Standalone libraries share the Flyology project identity but can be adopted without preparing or linking the runtime.

## Project structure

- **Core component:** Flyology Runtime provides native and lightweight task execution, task-aware I/O, and bounded systems building blocks.
- **Requires Flyology Runtime:** Flyology HTTP, Flyology Postgres, and Flyology QUIC.
- **Standalone:** Flyology Bench, Flyology Cachelines, Flyology Debug, Flyology IRI, Flyology SIMD, and Flyology TUI.

The dependency categories describe adoption, not importance. Use each component's linked documentation for its compiler, platform, maturity, verification, and licensing boundaries.

## Runtime vocabulary and boundaries

Flyology Runtime uses the terms **lightweight task** and **native task**. Both remain ordinary Ada tasks. Lightweight tasks run cooperatively on event loops in execution groups; native tasks remain on operating-system threads. Both lanes retain Ada rendezvous, protected objects, exceptions, activation, masters, task identity, and synchronous control flow.

Lightweight scheduling is cooperative, not preemptive. Flyology Runtime does not claim production qualification, universal portability, hard real-time behavior, or preemptive lightweight scheduling. Runtime preparation supports only the exact host and compiler release pairs documented by the project; do not infer support from the broader Alire dependency range.

## Add Flyology Runtime

Flyology is currently published through a separate Alire organization index. Keep the community index enabled for compiler and third-party dependencies, then add the Flyology index before it:

```sh
alr index --reset-community
alr index --add=git+https://github.com/flyology-ada/alire-index.git \
  --name=flyology --before=community
alr with flyology
```

This adds the `flyology` crate and its runtime preparation. Standalone components use their own crate names and do not prepare Flyology Runtime. The Flyology index is a development channel, not a community-index release. When Flyology is available from the community index, remove the development index with `alr index --del flyology`.

## Project documentation

- [Project overview](https://flyology.org/): Project purpose, component map, adoption paths, and shared boundaries.
- [Library directory](https://flyology.org/libraries/): Dependency category, Guide, API, website, and source links for each component.
- [Complete crate index](https://crates.flyology.org/): Every package published through the Flyology Alire index, including versions, dependencies, availability rules, manifests, JSON records, and compiler builds.
- [Development journal](https://flyology.org/journal/): Flyology project records and links to component journals.
- [Source organization](https://github.com/flyology-ada): Repositories for Flyology Runtime and independently maintained libraries.

## Flyology Runtime documentation

- [Runtime overview](https://flyology.org/runtime/): Execution model, included building blocks, status, and runtime constraints.
- [Runtime guide](https://flyology.org/guide/): Toolchain requirements, runtime preparation, task designation, stack and memory policy, execution groups, task-aware I/O, resource budgets, observability, verification, and constraints.
- [Runtime architecture](https://flyology.org/architecture/): GNAT tasking integration, native and lightweight lanes, schedulers, pollers, stackful contexts, memory ownership, and lifecycle boundaries.
- [Runtime API reference](https://flyology.org/api/): Generated reference for the main `flyology` crate. This is the API entry under the Runtime navigation, not an aggregate of every Flyology component.

### Runtime topic guides

- [Shared-memory segments](https://flyology.org/guide/shared-memory/): Anonymous, named POSIX, and file-backed storage; mapping and descriptor ownership; SCM_RIGHTS handoff; teardown; trust; blocking; and recovery limits.
- [Relocatable data structures](https://flyology.org/guide/data-structures/): Caller-owned backing regions, address-independent layouts, selectable arena allocation, bounded containers, synchronization models, attachment, relocation, poisoning, and recovery boundaries.
- [File watching](https://flyology.org/guide/file-watching/): Bounded file, directory, and recursive-tree registrations; task-aware waits; reconciliation; invalidation; and lost-event recovery.
- [File-to-socket transfers](https://flyology.org/guide/file-transfers/): Positional regular-file transfers, buffer ownership, deadlines, cancellation, native sendfile, Linux lightweight SEND_ZC, and fallbacks.
- [Native subprocesses](https://flyology.org/guide/subprocesses/): Native-task process creation, bounded capture, deadlines, cancellation, ownership, and teardown.
- [Structured task supervision](https://flyology.org/guide/supervision/): Typed static trees, bounded dynamic families, readiness, generation-safe replacement, recovery, incident budgets, stopping, and event rings.
- [Timers and clock changes](https://flyology.org/guide/timers/): Relative, monotonic, bounded multi-deadline, and wall-clock timer behavior, including backward clock changes.

## Libraries that require Flyology Runtime

- **Flyology HTTP:** [Website](https://http.flyology.org/), [Guide](https://http.flyology.org/guide/), [API](https://http.flyology.org/api/), [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology-http). HTTP/1.1 clients and servers, with opt-in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 engines and WebSocket support.
- **Flyology Postgres:** [Website](https://postgres.flyology.org/), [Guide](https://postgres.flyology.org/guide/), [Protocol API](https://postgres.flyology.org/api/), [SQL API](https://postgres.flyology.org/sql-api/), [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology-postgres). Client and server primitives for the Postgres frontend/backend protocol.
- **Flyology QUIC:** [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology-http/tree/main/flyology_quic). Experimental bounded QUIC transport with protocol state, streams, recovery, and congestion control. It does not currently publish a separate Guide or API site.

## Standalone libraries

- **Flyology Bench:** [Guide](https://flyology.org/guide/benchmarking/), [API](https://flyology.org/api/flyology_bench/), [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology/tree/main/flyology_bench). Adaptive microbenchmarking, balanced comparisons, diagnostics, baselines, and machine-readable reports.
- **Flyology Cachelines:** [Guide](https://flyology.org/guide/cachelines/), [API](https://flyology.org/api/flyology_cachelines/), [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology/tree/main/flyology_cachelines). Cache-line-aware storage, ownership-aware groups, grouped arrays, and host cache queries.
- **Flyology Debug:** [API](https://flyology.org/api/flyology_debug/), [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology/tree/main/flyology_debug). Bounded in-memory tracing, producer shards, retained batches, and persistent gauges.
- **Flyology IRI:** [Guide](https://http.flyology.org/guide/iri/), [API](https://http.flyology.org/iri-api/), [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology-http/tree/main/flyology_iri). Allocation-conscious URI, IRI, and WHATWG URL parsing.
- **Flyology NUMA:** [Guide](https://flyology.org/guide/numa/), [API](https://flyology.org/api/flyology_numa/), [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology/tree/main/flyology_numa). Memory-node reporting, memory placement on a chosen node, and node-bound storage pools.
- **Flyology SIMD:** [Website](https://simd.flyology.org/), [Guide](https://simd.flyology.org/guide/), [API](https://simd.flyology.org/api/), [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology-simd). Portable, strongly typed SIMD foundations for Ada.
- **Flyology TUI:** [Website](https://tui.flyology.org/), [Guide](https://tui.flyology.org/guide/), [API](https://tui.flyology.org/api/), [Source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology-tui). Typed, declarative terminal user-interface toolkit for Ada.

## Project sources

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flyology-ada/flyology/main/README.md): Detailed user-facing architecture, configuration, APIs, examples, constraints, and verification commands.
- [Runtime and bundled-library source](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology): Ada sources, runtime integration, standalone Bench, Cachelines, and Debug crates, tests, proofs, scripts, showcases, and website sources.
- [Supported runtime patch matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flyology-ada/flyology/main/runtime/patches/README.md): Exact verified host, compiler, and GNAT runtime patch families.
- [Alire crate manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flyology-ada/flyology/main/alire.toml): Package metadata and dependency constraints; these constraints are broader than the verified Runtime matrix.
